newsitem.title: USA: Graduate Health System, Pa. says cut 90 from staff.
newsitem.headline: Graduate Health System, Pa. says cut 90 from staff.

text.p: Philadelphia-based Graduate Health System said it cut about 90 employees from its four hospitals and its corporate offices.
Robert Mathews, Graduate's president, said the layoffs were part of an overall cost cutting plan developed over the past several months.
"These staff reductions, unfortunately, were needed to begin meeting these cost reductions goals," Mathews said in a statement.
Mathews said the extent of the layoffs vary from facility to facility. Graduate's four-hospital system comprises The Graduate Hospital, Mt Sinai Hospital, City Avenue Hospital, and Parkview Hospital.
Graduate recently announced plans to consolidate with the Allegheny Health, Education and Research Foundation. But Mathews said the layoffs were not related to the consolidation.

Moody's Investors Service last month downgraded Graduate's $170 million of outstanding debt to Ba from Baa, citing the uncertain long-term impact of a decision by Blue Cross to terminate various contracts with Graduate.
Standard & Poor's Corp rates the bonds BBB-plus.

In an analysis of the credit last month, Merrill Lynch & Co said the Allegheny move might be helpful for Graduate in the longrun, in part because of Allegheny's history of turning around distressed facilities.
But Merrill also warned that in the near term the credit could be hurt by disruptions caused by the consolidation.
